name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU][Cleanup] Decide the enabled autotune backends in one place

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU][Cleanup] Decide the enabled autotune backends in one place

Which autotune backends are enabled was decided in three places: in
`ConfigAssignerPass::GetEnabledBackends`, in the instruction filter of
`ConfigAssignerPass` (which derived again from the flags whether the
block-level emitter is enabled), and in the scaled-dot checks of `GpuCompiler`.
Each copy implemented a different subset of the rules, so they could disagree.

Make `GetEnabledBackendTypes` the only place that decides which backends are
enabled, and use its result everywhere else:

- `ConfigAssignerPass::CreateBackends` creates the backends of the given types.
  It replaces `GetEnabledBackends`.
- `GetShouldAssignConfigToInstructionFn` takes the enabled backends.
- The scaled-dot checks of `GpuCompiler` check whether the `TRITON` or
  `CUDNN_FISSION` backend is enabled.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018215911

display_title: Add an AOT compatibility golden for DynamicSliceFusionThunk

head_commit.message:
Add an AOT compatibility golden for DynamicSliceFusionThunk

DynamicSliceFusionThunk had no AOT compatibility golden, so a break in its
serialization or deserialization went unnoticed. It gets its own single-GPU
target, `dynamic_slice_fusion_aot_test`.

The case is a dot on one slice of a stacked weight array per loop iteration,
as in a `lax.scan` over layers. DynamicSliceFusionRewriterV2 wraps the
cuBLASLt matmul so that it reads the weight slice and writes the output slice
in place. The thunk itself only computes slice addresses and runs its embedded
thunk on them, so one case with a sliced operand and result and
loop-dependent offsets covers its runtime code.

display_title: [XLA] Fix SpaceToBatchConverter crash on backprop filter convs without overlap.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fix SpaceToBatchConverter crash on backprop filter convs without overlap.

PropagateOnBackpropFilterConv builds one activation chunk per output position
along the split dimension: low padding slices, original activations, then high
padding slices shifted from the last chunk. When the dilated kernel spans the
whole split dimension (overlap_count <= 0) and there is no low padding, no chunk
exists before the high padding loop, which then calls back() on an empty vector.

Always emit at least one original chunk when there is no low padding, and count
it in the number of high padding slices. HLO is unchanged for all previously
working cases.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018122743

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Fold exact bf16/f16 widening converts into f32 dots on GPU

head_commit.message:
Fold exact bf16/f16 widening converts into f32 dots on GPU

`f32 dot(convert<f32>(x:bf16), convert<f32>(y:bf16))` runs as a TF32 (or slower) GEMM and materializes the f32 operands, even though bf16/f16 values are exactly representable in f32 and TF32 and the products are exact in f32. So the dot can read the narrow operands directly and accumulate in f32 on bf16/f16 tensor cores.

`GpuAlgebraicSimplifier` now rewrites it to `f32 dot(x:bf16, y:bf16)` when the precision config is DEFAULT with no explicit algorithm, TF32 execution is enabled (so we never use tensor cores where the user opted out of them), the dot is cuBLAS-supported and above the GEMM rewrite size threshold, and the GPU supports the narrow type (Ampere+ for bf16, Volta+ for f16; MI300/RDNA3+ for bf16 on ROCm, where subnormals are preserved).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015885896

display_title: [ROCm] Port StreamExecutor test cases and fix the gaps they expose

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Port StreamExecutor test cases and fix the gaps they expose

- RocmExecutor::IsHostMemoryPinned left start_addr/range_size
  uninitialized when hipDrvPointerGetAttributes does not populate them,
  so the containment check read indeterminate stack values.

- RocmExecutor::GetPointerMemorySpace returned InternalError for
  hipMallocManaged memory. It now queries HIP_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_IS_MANAGED
  first and maps managed/unified memory types to MemorySpace::kUnified

- RocmStream only declared the single-argument DoHostCallbackWithStatus,
  which name-hid the error_cb overload and silently dropped asynchronous
  callback failures. The overload is now implemented, including invoking
  error_cb when the callback cannot be enqueued.

Test cases added:
  rocm_kernel_test:   ArityZeroKernelSkipsArgumentCountCheck
  rocm_executor_test: IsHostMemoryPinnedWorksWithRegisteredHostMemory
                      GetPointerMemorySpaceWorksWithUnifiedMemory
  rocm_stream_test:   DoHostCallbackWithStatusSuccess
                      DoHostCallbackWithStatusError

display_title: Add an AOT compatibility golden for DynamicSliceFusionThunk

head_commit.message:
Add an AOT compatibility golden for DynamicSliceFusionThunk

DynamicSliceFusionThunk had no AOT compatibility golden, so a break in its
serialization or deserialization went unnoticed. It gets its own single-GPU
target, `dynamic_slice_fusion_aot_test`.

The case is a dot on one slice of a stacked weight array per loop iteration,
as in a `lax.scan` over layers. DynamicSliceFusionRewriterV2 wraps the
cuBLASLt matmul so that it reads the weight slice and writes the output slice
in place. The thunk itself only computes slice addresses and runs its embedded
thunk on them, so one case with a sliced operand and result and
loop-dependent offsets covers its runtime code.

display_title: [XLA:TSL] Reject negative byte counts in SnappyInputStream

head_commit.message:
[XLA:TSL] Reject negative byte counts in SnappyInputStream

SnappyInputStream::ReadNBytes passed a negative bytes_to_read to
tstring::resize_uninitialized, which takes a size_t. A count of -1 hit
the __builtin_trap in TF_TString_ResizeUninitialized and killed the
process; other negative counts convert to a size of 2^63 or more.
BufferedInputStream and RandomAccessInputStream return InvalidArgument
for a negative count.

Return InvalidArgument from SnappyInputStream::ReadNBytes the same way,
leaving result empty. Add tests for rejection, which also checks that
the stream stays usable at the same position, and for zero and
positive counts.

Follow-up to #52502.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Widen interval indices and element counts to int64_t in CoalescingAnalysis

`FindIntervals`, `FindContiguousIntervals`, and `EstimateCoalescingViaMemoryTransactionsCount` in `xla/service/gpu/model/coalescing_analysis.cc` previously narrowed 64-bit linear indices, warp stride offsets, element counts, and memory transaction counts to 32-bit `int`. When linearized input indices or contiguous interval lengths exceed `INT32_MAX`, `FindIntervals` failed to merge contiguous indices and `EstimateCoalescingViaMemoryTransactionsCount` overflowed `total_num_elements`, falsely reporting coalesced reads as uncoalesced. Widen these variables to `int64_t`.

head_commit.message:
PR #51549: [XLA:GPU] Cost-weight ragged all-to-all LSA copy by destination

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51549

📝 Summary of Changes
Makes the ragged a2a device kernel's LSA copy loop cost-aware: CTAs are assigned to transfers proportionally to how much time each transfer takes, rather than uniformly.

🎯 Justification
Uniform CTA assignment leaves the fastest transfers idle waiting for the slowest. On heterogeneous ragged workloads (different peers get different amounts of data, different types of transfer), cost-weighted assignment matches CTA count to the work each transfer represents. The additional regime switch chooses between the fabric-bound and NVLink-bound cost models based on `RaggedAllToAllRemoteCost`.

`FindIntervals`, `FindContiguousIntervals`, and `EstimateCoalescingViaMemoryTransactionsCount` in `xla/service/gpu/model/coalescing_analysis.cc` previously narrowed 64-bit linear indices, warp stride offsets, element counts, and memory transaction counts to 32-bit `int`. When linearized input indices or contiguous interval lengths exceed `INT32_MAX`, `FindIntervals` failed to merge contiguous indices and `EstimateCoalescingViaMemoryTransactionsCount` overflowed `total_num_elements`, falsely reporting coalesced reads as uncoalesced. Widen these variables to `int64_t`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Model epilogue operand reads and writes outside the pipelined K loop.

`GpuIndexingPerformanceModel` previously passed all fusion operand reads (with
`include_cache_rereads=false`) and output writes into
`CalculatePipelinedLoopTimeWithLaunchWaves`. However, epilogue operand reads and
output writes run after the K-loop completes and cannot be hidden by K-loop
software pipelining, and `CalculateL2Time` only models L2 traffic for dot-region
operands.

Charge epilogue operand reads (with cache re-reads enabled) and output writes
after the pipelined mainloop rather than inside the K-loop.

head_commit.message:
PR #52527: [XLA:GPU] Forbid parameter-only reducers in Triton reduce support and fix reduce lowering

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52527

`(a, b) -> b` reducers (JAX's "take last") fail to compile once they land in a Triton normalization fusion:

```
INTERNAL: RET_CHECK failure (emitter_helpers.cc:1255) !to_emit.empty()
```

In XTile's `EmitReduceWithNoRegion` and `EmitReduceWithRegion`, out-of-bounds lanes at the end of a padded power-of-2 tile are masked with `neutral_value = init_value` via `xtile::MaskOp`. That assumes `init_value` is a right-identity of the combiner (`f(x, init_value) == x`), which does not hold for parameter-only reducers like `(a, b) -> b` (`f(x, init_value) = init_value`), causing padded reduction dimensions to silently return `init_value`.

Changes in this PR:
- **Forbid parameter-only reducers in Triton support**: `CanTritonHandleReduce` now forbids reducers whose root instruction is `kParameter`, so they fall back to the native emitter. `SupportTest.ParameterOnlyReducerFailsGracefullyWithTriton` checks both the `Forbid` decision and that codegen rejects the computation.
- **Fix accumulator/element mapping in `LowerReduce`**: `CombineReduceResultsWithInitValues` previously mapped `(arg i -> reduce result, arg N+i -> init)` in reverse order. Swap the mapping so the accumulator (`arg i`) is mapped to `init` and the element (`arg N+i`) to the `tt.reduce` result, and add a regression test in `stable_hlo_to_triton_lowering.mlir`.
- **Keep the XTile emitter failing instead of emitting these reducers**: `EmitScope` now rejects an empty instruction list, so a parameter-only combiner that reaches the emitter (bypassing the support check) fails with a status instead of miscompiling padded tiles.

Fixes #50830.

ea8d2c614d5b72855690ab58776fa250b3e1956a by Iris <244965872+BlueIrisSky@users.noreply.github.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Forbid parameter-only reducers in Triton reduce support

Lanes past the end of a tile are masked with the reduction's init value, which
assumes that the init value is neutral for the combiner. A combiner that just
returns one of its parameters, e.g. the `(a, b) -> b` combiner of a "take last"
reduction, has no such neutral value: every padded reduction dimension returned
the init value instead of the last element.

Forbid these computations in `CanTritonHandleReduce` so that the fusion falls
back to the native emitter, and keep the XTile emitter rejecting an empty
combiner body (`EmitReduceComputation`, `EmitScope`, `EmitCombinerStep`), so
that callers which bypass the support check fail with a status instead of
silently miscompiling padded tiles. The CPU tiled backend rejects these
combiners as well, so nothing is lost there.

Also fix the accumulator/element mapping in `LowerReduce`
(stablehlo_lower_to_triton.cc): the tt.reduce result plays the element, the
init value the accumulator. The previous mapping collapsed parameter-only
reducers to the init value.

Tests:
 - `SupportTest.ParameterOnlyReducerFailsGracefullyWithTriton` checks both the
   `Forbid` decision and that codegen rejects the computation.
 - `SoftmaxRewriterTritonTest.DoesNotFuseDiamondWithParameterOnlyReducer`
   covers the `reduce -> broadcast -> multiply` diamond of #50830.
 - `@reduce_with_parameter_only_reducer_and_non_neutral_init` pins down the
   `LowerReduce` argument mapping.

Merging this change closes #52527

head_commit.message:
Add an AOT compatibility golden for DynamicSliceFusionThunk

DynamicSliceFusionThunk had no AOT compatibility golden, so a break in its
serialization or deserialization went unnoticed. It gets its own single-GPU
target, `dynamic_slice_fusion_aot_test`.

The case is a dot on one slice of a stacked weight array per loop iteration,
as in a `lax.scan` over layers. DynamicSliceFusionRewriterV2 wraps the
cuBLASLt matmul so that it reads the weight slice and writes the output slice
in place. The thunk itself only computes slice addresses and runs its embedded
thunk on them, so one case with a sliced operand and result and
loop-dependent offsets covers its runtime code.

head_commit.message:
PR #51549: [XLA:GPU] Cost-weight ragged all-to-all LSA copy by destination

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51549

📝 Summary of Changes
Makes the ragged a2a device kernel's LSA copy loop cost-aware: CTAs are assigned to transfers proportionally to how much time each transfer takes, rather than uniformly.

🎯 Justification
Uniform CTA assignment leaves the fastest transfers idle waiting for the slowest. On heterogeneous ragged workloads (different peers get different amounts of data, different types of transfer), cost-weighted assignment matches CTA count to the work each transfer represents. The additional regime switch chooses between the fabric-bound and NVLink-bound cost models based on `RaggedAllToAllRemoteCost`.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
⚡️ Performance Improvement

display_title: Use CompilationProvider in CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx

head_commit.message:
Use CompilationProvider in CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx

`CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx` previously compiled PTX via `cuModuleLoadDataEx` on the single-threaded `cuda_driver` thread pool, which serialized PTX compilation across GPUs.

So this change replaces `LoadPtx` with a process-wide `CachingCompilationProvider` in `CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx` and loads the resulting CUBIN with `LoadCubin`. This avoids the single-threaded driver JIT and compiles each PTX module once per compute capability across all GPUs on a host.

Also:

1. Only retain `stream_exec_` in `CompilationProviderOptions` when driver compilation is enabled, and include `stream_exec_` in `operator==` so it matches `AbslHashValue`.
2. Remove the spurious `.extern` qualifier on the fixed-size `global_smem` array in `GetTmaPtxKernelSpec` so relocatable compilation providers can link it.
3. Clamp the target compute capability to the major architecture baseline (e.g. `sm_100` on `sm_103a`) when the compilation provider's PTX ISA version is older than the GPU's compute capability.

Use CompilationProvider in CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx

`CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx` previously compiled PTX via `cuModuleLoadDataEx` on the single-threaded `cuda_driver` thread pool, which serialized PTX compilation across GPUs.

So this change replaces `LoadPtx` with a process-wide `CachingCompilationProvider` in `CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx` and loads the resulting CUBIN with `LoadCubin`. This avoids the single-threaded driver JIT and compiles each PTX module once per compute capability across all GPUs on a host.

Also:

1. Only retain `stream_exec_` in `CompilationProviderOptions` when driver compilation is enabled, and include `stream_exec_` in `operator==` so it matches `AbslHashValue`.
2. Remove the spurious `.extern` qualifier on the fixed-size `global_smem` array in `GetTmaPtxKernelSpec` so relocatable compilation providers can link it.
3. Clamp the target compute capability to the major architecture baseline (e.g. `sm_100` on `sm_103a`) when the compilation provider's PTX ISA version is older than the GPU's compute capability.

display_title: PR #52527: [XLA:GPU] Forbid parameter-only reducers in Triton reduce support and fix reduce lowering

head_commit.message:
PR #52527: [XLA:GPU] Forbid parameter-only reducers in Triton reduce support and fix reduce lowering

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52527

`(a, b) -> b` reducers (JAX's "take last") fail to compile once they land in a Triton normalization fusion:

```
INTERNAL: RET_CHECK failure (emitter_helpers.cc:1255) !to_emit.empty()
```

In XTile's `EmitReduceWithNoRegion` and `EmitReduceWithRegion`, out-of-bounds lanes at the end of a padded power-of-2 tile are masked with `neutral_value = init_value` via `xtile::MaskOp`. That assumes `init_value` is a right-identity of the combiner (`f(x, init_value) == x`), which does not hold for parameter-only reducers like `(a, b) -> b` (`f(x, init_value) = init_value`), causing padded reduction dimensions to silently return `init_value`.

Changes in this PR:
- **Forbid parameter-only reducers in Triton support**: `CanTritonHandleReduce` now forbids reducers whose root instruction is `kParameter`, so they fall back to the native emitter. `SupportTest.ParameterOnlyReducerFailsGracefullyWithTriton` checks both the `Forbid` decision and that codegen rejects the computation.
- **Fix accumulator/element mapping in `LowerReduce`**: `CombineReduceResultsWithInitValues` previously mapped `(arg i -> reduce result, arg N+i -> init)` in reverse order. Swap the mapping so the accumulator (`arg i`) is mapped to `init` and the element (`arg N+i`) to the `tt.reduce` result, and add a regression test in `stable_hlo_to_triton_lowering.mlir`.
- **Keep the XTile emitter failing instead of emitting these reducers**: `EmitScope` now rejects an empty instruction list, so a parameter-only combiner that reaches the emitter (bypassing the support check) fails with a status instead of miscompiling padded tiles.

Fixes #50830.

Copybara import of the project:

--
ea8d2c614d5b72855690ab58776fa250b3e1956a by Iris <244965872+BlueIrisSky@users.noreply.github.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Forbid parameter-only reducers in Triton reduce support

Lanes past the end of a tile are masked with the reduction's init value, which
assumes that the init value is neutral for the combiner. A combiner that just
returns one of its parameters, e.g. the `(a, b) -> b` combiner of a "take last"
reduction, has no such neutral value: every padded reduction dimension returned
the init value instead of the last element.

Forbid these computations in `CanTritonHandleReduce` so that the fusion falls
back to the native emitter, and keep the XTile emitter rejecting an empty
combiner body (`EmitReduceComputation`, `EmitScope`, `EmitCombinerStep`), so
that callers which bypass the support check fail with a status instead of
silently miscompiling padded tiles. The CPU tiled backend rejects these
combiners as well, so nothing is lost there.

Also fix the accumulator/element mapping in `LowerReduce`
(stablehlo_lower_to_triton.cc): the tt.reduce result plays the element, the
init value the accumulator. The previous mapping collapsed parameter-only
reducers to the init value.

Tests:
 - `SupportTest.ParameterOnlyReducerFailsGracefullyWithTriton` checks both the
   `Forbid` decision and that codegen rejects the computation.
 - `SoftmaxRewriterTritonTest.DoesNotFuseDiamondWithParameterOnlyReducer`
   covers the `reduce -> broadcast -> multiply` diamond of #50830.
 - `@reduce_with_parameter_only_reducer_and_non_neutral_init` pins down the
   `LowerReduce` argument mapping.

Merging this change closes #52527

display_title: PR #51088: [ROCm] Add libomp.so to the hipblaslt runtime data for ROCm 10.2 only!

head_commit.message:
PR #51088: [ROCm] Add libomp.so to the hipblaslt runtime data for ROCm 10.2 only!

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51088

## What

Add `rocm_path("lib/llvm/lib/libomp.so*")` to the `hipblaslt` runtime data in `third_party/gpus/rocm/BUILD.tpl`, next to `libtensilelite-host.so*`. The ROCm 10.2 release keeps this dependency; later ROCm builds no longer link OpenMP into `libtensilelite-host`.

## Why

In ROCm 10.2, `libhipblaslt.so.1` depends on `libtensilelite-host.so.1`, which needs `libomp.so` and finds it through `$ORIGIN/llvm/lib`. #50239 added `libtensilelite-host.so*` to the `hipblaslt` data but not `libomp.so`, so `rocm_dist/lib/llvm/lib/libomp.so` is missing from runfiles and anything that loads hipBLASLt from a 10.2 install fails before `main`:

```
error while loading shared libraries: libomp.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

This currently breaks the ROCm 10.2 nightly test runs, including the JAX unit tests in ROCm/xla's CI, where `xla_rocm_plugin.so` fails to load and every GPU test falls back to "Unknown backend: 'gpu'". ROCm 10.0 is unaffected because none of its math libraries need `libomp`.

## Testing

A `cc_test` depending on `@local_config_rocm//rocm:hipblaslt` that calls `dlopen("libhipblaslt.so.1", RTLD_NOW)`, built with `--config=rocm` and `ROCM_PATH` set to the TheRock pip install (`rocm-sdk path --root`), in the rocmless CI image:

| ROCm | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 10.2.0a20261016 | fails: `libomp.so: cannot open shared object file` | passes; `libomp.so` loads next to `libtensilelite-host.so.1` |
| 10.0.0 | n/a | passes |

End to end: jax-ml/jax `main` Bazel GPU tests (`build/rocm/ci_test_targets.txt`, `--//jax:build_jaxlib=wheel`, the ROCm/xla CI flags without RBE) on a local gfx950 with TheRock 10.2.0a20261016 from pip and this change applied via `--override_repository=xla`: 147 of 147 tests pass. Reverting this change, `//tests:cholesky_update_test_gpu` fails with `libomp.so: cannot open shared object file`, as in CI.

`--incompatible_disallow_empty_glob=false` is set in both XLA's and JAX's `.bazelrc`, so ROCm installs without `libomp` are unaffected.

Copybara import of the project:

--

libtensilelite-host.so needs libomp.so and finds it through $ORIGIN/llvm/lib. Without libomp in runfiles, binaries that load hipBLASLt from ROCm 10.2 fail with "libomp.so: cannot open shared object file".

Merging this change closes #51088

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix HBM derating and widened L2 traffic in dot cost model.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix HBM derating and widened L2 traffic in dot cost model.

Previously, `GpuIndexingPerformanceModel` multiplied the per-tile coalescing
utilization rate by the transfer-size HBM derate on dot fusions, compounding
both penalties on small GEMMs into an unrealistically low effective bandwidth.
Take the minimum of the two rates instead and apply it in floating point.

In addition, when a fused prologue widens narrow inputs (such as `s8 -> bf16`),
counting only fusion parameter reads under-estimates K-loop L2 traffic by 2x
and causes slow widening fusions to beat cuBLASLt. Bound L2 traffic below by
the masked dot-operand tile reads across the K-loop.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018084428

display_title: Fix variadic scatter output-index matching in HloDataflowAnalysis

head_commit.message:
Fix variadic scatter output-index matching in HloDataflowAnalysis

For a bare variadic `scatter` whose inputs have the same shape, `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` falls past the must-alias check when `user_index` points to another output tuple element, and then only checked `operand_indices[0] == 0`. That wrongly allowed input 0 to share its buffer with output `{1}`. Match `operand_indices[0]` against `user_index[0]` for tuple-shaped scatters instead.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Model pipelined loop and L2 cache timing for tiled dot fusions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Model pipelined loop and L2 cache timing for tiled dot fusions.

Previously, `GpuIndexingPerformanceModel` evaluated each dot in isolation via
`EstimateRunTimeForDotOpWithBlockParameters`—using HBM and L2 traffic derived
only from the dot's immediate operands—and combined it with the fusion runtime
via `max(exec_time, dot_exec_time)`.

Instead, accumulate mainloop compute time and K-loop iterations across dots in
the fusion, and compute pipelined K-loop timing across launch waves and L2
cache timing at the fusion level using the fusion's actual DRAM transfer times
and dot-region L2 bytes read.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018073939

display_title: PR #51088: [ROCm] Add libomp.so to the hipblaslt runtime data for ROCm 10.2 only!

head_commit.message:
PR #51088: [ROCm] Add libomp.so to the hipblaslt runtime data for ROCm 10.2 only!

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51088

## What

Add `rocm_path("lib/llvm/lib/libomp.so*")` to the `hipblaslt` runtime data in `third_party/gpus/rocm/BUILD.tpl`, next to `libtensilelite-host.so*`. The ROCm 10.2 release keeps this dependency; later ROCm builds no longer link OpenMP into `libtensilelite-host`.

## Why

In ROCm 10.2, `libhipblaslt.so.1` depends on `libtensilelite-host.so.1`, which needs `libomp.so` and finds it through `$ORIGIN/llvm/lib`. #50239 added `libtensilelite-host.so*` to the `hipblaslt` data but not `libomp.so`, so `rocm_dist/lib/llvm/lib/libomp.so` is missing from runfiles and anything that loads hipBLASLt from a 10.2 install fails before `main`:

```
error while loading shared libraries: libomp.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

This currently breaks the ROCm 10.2 nightly test runs, including the JAX unit tests in ROCm/xla's CI, where `xla_rocm_plugin.so` fails to load and every GPU test falls back to "Unknown backend: 'gpu'". ROCm 10.0 is unaffected because none of its math libraries need `libomp`.

## Testing

A `cc_test` depending on `@local_config_rocm//rocm:hipblaslt` that calls `dlopen("libhipblaslt.so.1", RTLD_NOW)`, built with `--config=rocm` and `ROCM_PATH` set to the TheRock pip install (`rocm-sdk path --root`), in the rocmless CI image:

| ROCm | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 10.2.0a20261016 | fails: `libomp.so: cannot open shared object file` | passes; `libomp.so` loads next to `libtensilelite-host.so.1` |
| 10.0.0 | n/a | passes |

End to end: jax-ml/jax `main` Bazel GPU tests (`build/rocm/ci_test_targets.txt`, `--//jax:build_jaxlib=wheel`, the ROCm/xla CI flags without RBE) on a local gfx950 with TheRock 10.2.0a20261016 from pip and this change applied via `--override_repository=xla`: 147 of 147 tests pass. Reverting this change, `//tests:cholesky_update_test_gpu` fails with `libomp.so: cannot open shared object file`, as in CI.

`--incompatible_disallow_empty_glob=false` is set in both XLA's and JAX's `.bazelrc`, so ROCm installs without `libomp` are unaffected.

Copybara import of the project:

--
c95b6b5f418254a324a032bfb907fd4459af267a by gulsumgudukbay <gudukbay@gmail.com>:

[ROCm] Add libomp.so to the hipblaslt runtime data

libtensilelite-host.so needs libomp.so and finds it through $ORIGIN/llvm/lib. Without libomp in runfiles, binaries that load hipBLASLt from ROCm 10.2 fail with "libomp.so: cannot open shared object file".

Merging this change closes #51088

display_title: PR #52527: [XLA:GPU] Forbid parameter-only reducers in Triton reduce support and fix reduce lowering

head_commit.message:
PR #52527: [XLA:GPU] Forbid parameter-only reducers in Triton reduce support and fix reduce lowering

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52527

`(a, b) -> b` reducers (JAX's "take last") fail to compile once they land in a Triton normalization fusion:

```
INTERNAL: RET_CHECK failure (emitter_helpers.cc:1255) !to_emit.empty()
```

In XTile's `EmitReduceWithNoRegion` and `EmitReduceWithRegion`, out-of-bounds lanes at the end of a padded power-of-2 tile are masked with `neutral_value = init_value` via `xtile::MaskOp`. That assumes `init_value` is a right-identity of the combiner (`f(x, init_value) == x`), which does not hold for parameter-only reducers like `(a, b) -> b` (`f(x, init_value) = init_value`), causing padded reduction dimensions to silently return `init_value`.

Changes in this PR:
- **Forbid parameter-only reducers in Triton support**: `CanTritonHandleReduce` now forbids reducers whose root instruction is `kParameter`, so they fall back to the native emitter. `SupportTest.ParameterOnlyReducerFailsGracefullyWithTriton` checks both the `Forbid` decision and that codegen rejects the computation.
- **Fix accumulator/element mapping in `LowerReduce`**: `CombineReduceResultsWithInitValues` previously mapped `(arg i -> reduce result, arg N+i -> init)` in reverse order. Swap the mapping so the accumulator (`arg i`) is mapped to `init` and the element (`arg N+i`) to the `tt.reduce` result, and add a regression test in `stable_hlo_to_triton_lowering.mlir`.
- **Keep the XTile emitter failing instead of emitting these reducers**: `EmitScope` now rejects an empty instruction list, so a parameter-only combiner that reaches the emitter (bypassing the support check) fails with a status instead of miscompiling padded tiles.

Fixes #50830.

Copybara import of the project:

--

Lanes past the end of a tile are masked with the reduction's init value, which
assumes that the init value is neutral for the combiner. A combiner that just
returns one of its parameters, e.g. the `(a, b) -> b` combiner of a "take last"
reduction, has no such neutral value: every padded reduction dimension returned
the init value instead of the last element.

Forbid these computations in `CanTritonHandleReduce` so that the fusion falls
back to the native emitter, and keep the XTile emitter rejecting an empty
combiner body (`EmitReduceComputation`, `EmitScope`, `EmitCombinerStep`), so
that callers which bypass the support check fail with a status instead of
silently miscompiling padded tiles. The CPU tiled backend rejects these
combiners as well, so nothing is lost there.

Also fix the accumulator/element mapping in `LowerReduce`
(stablehlo_lower_to_triton.cc): the tt.reduce result plays the element, the
init value the accumulator. The previous mapping collapsed parameter-only
reducers to the init value.

Tests:
 - `SupportTest.ParameterOnlyReducerFailsGracefullyWithTriton` checks both the
   `Forbid` decision and that codegen rejects the computation.
 - `SoftmaxRewriterTritonTest.DoesNotFuseDiamondWithParameterOnlyReducer`
   covers the `reduce -> broadcast -> multiply` diamond of #50830.
 - `@reduce_with_parameter_only_reducer_and_non_neutral_init` pins down the
   `LowerReduce` argument mapping.

Merging this change closes #52527

display_title: Fix variadic scatter output-index matching in HloDataflowAnalysis

head_commit.message:
Fix variadic scatter output-index matching in HloDataflowAnalysis

For a bare variadic `scatter` whose inputs have the same shape, `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` falls past the must-alias check when `user_index` points to another output tuple element, and then only checked `operand_indices[0] == 0`. That wrongly allowed input 0 to share its buffer with output `{1}`. Match `operand_indices[0]` against `user_index[0]` for tuple-shaped scatters instead.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Populate compute and memory utilization for tiled dot fusions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Populate compute and memory utilization for tiled dot fusions.

As part of migrating `gpu_dot_fusion_cost_model` into
`GpuIndexingPerformanceModel`, populate wave-quantized `compute_utilization` and
`memory_utilization` on `EstimateRunTimeData` for tiled dot fusions and add a
unit test covering pipelined K-loop stage overlap.

This matches the utilization calculation in
`EstimateRunTimeForDotOpWithBlockParameters` from `gpu_dot_fusion_cost_model`,
where utilization is defined as the ratio of wave-quantized compute or memory
time to total execution time, but derives memory time from the full fusion's L2
and HBM transfer estimates rather than the bare dot operands alone.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix HBM derating and widened L2 traffic in dot cost model.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix HBM derating and widened L2 traffic in dot cost model.

Previously, `GpuIndexingPerformanceModel` multiplied the per-tile coalescing
utilization rate by the transfer-size HBM derate on dot fusions, compounding
both penalties on small GEMMs into an unrealistically low effective bandwidth.
Take the minimum of the two rates instead and apply it in floating point.

In addition, when a fused prologue widens narrow inputs (such as `s8 -> bf16`),
counting only fusion parameter reads under-estimates K-loop L2 traffic by 2x
and causes slow widening fusions to beat cuBLASLt. Bound L2 traffic below by
the masked dot-operand tile reads across the K-loop.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1000319647

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Model pipelined loop and L2 cache timing for tiled dot fusions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Model pipelined loop and L2 cache timing for tiled dot fusions.

Previously, `GpuIndexingPerformanceModel` evaluated each dot in isolation via
`EstimateRunTimeForDotOpWithBlockParameters`—using HBM and L2 traffic derived
only from the dot's immediate operands—and combined it with the fusion runtime
via `max(exec_time, dot_exec_time)`.

Instead, accumulate mainloop compute time and K-loop iterations across dots in
the fusion, and compute pipelined K-loop timing across launch waves and L2
cache timing at the fusion level using the fusion's actual DRAM transfer times
and dot-region L2 bytes read.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 986896560

display_title: [IFRT IR] Null-terminate text atom programs before deserialization

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Null-terminate text atom programs before deserialization

`IfrtAtomProgramsFromVhloPass` passed a flattened `absl::Cord`, which is not null-terminated, to the MLIR parser. Atom programs are normally MLIR bytecode, but text input is parsed by the MLIR lexer, which assumes a null-terminated buffer and could read past the end of the atom program.

Copy the atom program to a `std::string` when it is not MLIR bytecode. Bytecode is still deserialized without a copy.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018058793

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Clear dynamic slice configs in autotuning candidates.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Clear dynamic slice configs in autotuning candidates.

A `DynamicSliceConfig` lets the runtime compute a slice offset from the
enclosing while loop's iteration instead of the offset operands. Autotuning
compiles candidates in standalone modules without that loop, so the runtime
used iteration 0 and ignored the operands. This made the cuBLASLt fission
reference read the wrong slice when the parameter was non-zero and all Triton
candidates fail the correctness check, even though they were reading the
correct slice. Clear these configs in candidate modules; the original module is
unchanged.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/52255

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018058611

display_title: PR #51088: [ROCm] Add libomp.so to the hipblaslt runtime data for ROCm 10.2 only!

head_commit.message:
PR #51088: [ROCm] Add libomp.so to the hipblaslt runtime data for ROCm 10.2 only!

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51088

## What

Add `rocm_path("lib/llvm/lib/libomp.so*")` to the `hipblaslt` runtime data in `third_party/gpus/rocm/BUILD.tpl`, next to `libtensilelite-host.so*`. The ROCm 10.2 release keeps this dependency; later ROCm builds no longer link OpenMP into `libtensilelite-host`.

## Why

In ROCm 10.2, `libhipblaslt.so.1` depends on `libtensilelite-host.so.1`, which needs `libomp.so` and finds it through `$ORIGIN/llvm/lib`. #50239 added `libtensilelite-host.so*` to the `hipblaslt` data but not `libomp.so`, so `rocm_dist/lib/llvm/lib/libomp.so` is missing from runfiles and anything that loads hipBLASLt from a 10.2 install fails before `main`:

```
error while loading shared libraries: libomp.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

This currently breaks the ROCm 10.2 nightly test runs, including the JAX unit tests in ROCm/xla's CI, where `xla_rocm_plugin.so` fails to load and every GPU test falls back to "Unknown backend: 'gpu'". ROCm 10.0 is unaffected because none of its math libraries need `libomp`.

## Testing

A `cc_test` depending on `@local_config_rocm//rocm:hipblaslt` that calls `dlopen("libhipblaslt.so.1", RTLD_NOW)`, built with `--config=rocm` and `ROCM_PATH` set to the TheRock pip install (`rocm-sdk path --root`), in the rocmless CI image:

| ROCm | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 10.2.0a20261016 | fails: `libomp.so: cannot open shared object file` | passes; `libomp.so` loads next to `libtensilelite-host.so.1` |
| 10.0.0 | n/a | passes |

End to end: jax-ml/jax `main` Bazel GPU tests (`build/rocm/ci_test_targets.txt`, `--//jax:build_jaxlib=wheel`, the ROCm/xla CI flags without RBE) on a local gfx950 with TheRock 10.2.0a20261016 from pip and this change applied via `--override_repository=xla`: 147 of 147 tests pass. Reverting this change, `//tests:cholesky_update_test_gpu` fails with `libomp.so: cannot open shared object file`, as in CI.

`--incompatible_disallow_empty_glob=false` is set in both XLA's and JAX's `.bazelrc`, so ROCm installs without `libomp` are unaffected.

Copybara import of the project:

--
c95b6b5f418254a324a032bfb907fd4459af267a by gulsumgudukbay <gudukbay@gmail.com>:

[ROCm] Add libomp.so to the hipblaslt runtime data

libtensilelite-host.so needs libomp.so and finds it through $ORIGIN/llvm/lib. Without libomp in runfiles, binaries that load hipBLASLt from ROCm 10.2 fail with "libomp.so: cannot open shared object file".

Merging this change closes #51088

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Preserve frontend attributes in GemmFusion

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Preserve frontend attributes in GemmFusion

GemmFusion now propagates the dot's metadata and frontend attributes onto the Triton fusion and, when the fusion's shape differs from the dot's, onto the bitcast that replaces the dot, so annotations are not dropped.

If the fused instructions carry conflicting scheduling annotations (e.g. the dot and its epilogue are in different scheduling groups), the fusion and its replacement are left without a scheduling annotation, so LegalizeSchedulingAnnotations still reports the conflict instead of the dot's group silently winning.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] [2/2] Unroll and vectorize kLoop reductions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] [2/2] Unroll and vectorize kLoop reductions.

***Problem:*** `kLoop` fusions that loop over a small reduction dimension (e.g. split-K factors below the warp size) never get vectorized loads and stores, because the unroll factor is sized only from the small output element count and `VectorizeLoadsAndStoresPass` runs before the inner reduction loop is unrolled, so it only sees that non-unit-stride loop.

***Solution:*** Allow unrolling up to `MaxUnrollFactor` (while keeping enough threads to fill the GPU) when the fusion contains a `kReduce` whose operand alone can saturate the GPU, unroll only the inner reduction loops before `VectorizeLoadsAndStoresPass` so the outer unroll loop becomes the innermost vectorizable loop, and teach `lower_tensors` to infer access alignment from `xla.apply_indexing` indices.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007125473

display_title: PR #51724: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

head_commit.message:
PR #51724: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51724

📝 Summary of Changes

Implements the allocator layer that later PRs build the per-domain BFC pools on.

Adds `StreamExecutor::CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocator(int locality_domain_id)`, which returns a MemoryAllocator whose physical memory is placed on one locality domain (die) of a multi-die GPU.

CUDA implementation: `locality_domain_id` added to `CudaDeviceAllocator::Options`. When it's set, the allocator creates physical memory with `cuMemCreate` with location set to `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN`.

Errors instead of fallback: it rejects out-of-range domain IDs, CUDA older than 13.4, single-domain devices, and the cuMemAlloc path (use_vmm=false). It never falls back to whole-device memory.

🎯 Justification

This is the third PR in the locality-domain series ([first](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50131) and [second](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51429) PRs)

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature and 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A: this PR adds the allocator only. Performance benefits to be evaluated later.

🧪 Unit Tests:
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.RejectsOutOfRangeLocalityDomain`: domain IDs below -1 or above 255 are rejected.
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.LocalityDomainRequiresCuda134`: CUDA older than 13.4 is rejected.
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.LocalityDomainRequiresVmm`: use_vmm=false is rejected.
- `CudaExecutorTest.CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocatorRejectsInvalidId`: IDs outside [0, domain_count) are rejected.
- `DeviceAddressVmmAllocatorTest.RejectsLocalityDomainMemorySpaces`: locality-domain colors are rejected on every allocation path.

🧪 Execution Tests:
Both run on a single GPU:

- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.PlacesMemoryOnEachDomain`: for each domain, allocates memory and checks with `cuMemGetAllocationPropertiesFromHandle` that its location is `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN` with the requested domain ID. Then it round-trips data host to device to host.
- `CudaExecutorTest.CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocatorWorks`: creates an allocator for every domain and allocates from it. On a single-domain GPU, it checks that creating one fails.

head_commit.message:
PR #51549: [XLA:GPU] Cost-weight ragged all-to-all LSA copy by destination

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51549

📝 Summary of Changes
Makes the ragged a2a device kernel's LSA copy loop cost-aware: CTAs are assigned to transfers proportionally to how much time each transfer takes, rather than uniformly.

🎯 Justification
Uniform CTA assignment leaves the fastest transfers idle waiting for the slowest. On heterogeneous ragged workloads (different peers get different amounts of data, different types of transfer), cost-weighted assignment matches CTA count to the work each transfer represents. The additional regime switch chooses between the fabric-bound and NVLink-bound cost models based on `RaggedAllToAllRemoteCost`.

display_title: Use CompilationProvider in CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx

head_commit.message:
Use CompilationProvider in CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx

`CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx` previously compiled PTX via `cuModuleLoadDataEx` on the single-threaded `cuda_driver` thread pool, which serialized PTX compilation across GPUs.

So this change replaces `LoadPtx` with a process-wide `CachingCompilationProvider` in `CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx` and loads the resulting CUBIN with `LoadCubin`. This avoids the single-threaded driver JIT and compiles each PTX module once per compute capability across all GPUs on a host.

Also:

1. Only retain `stream_exec_` in `CompilationProviderOptions` when driver compilation is enabled, and include `stream_exec_` in `operator==` so it matches `AbslHashValue`.
2. Remove the spurious `.extern` qualifier on the fixed-size `global_smem` array in `GetTmaPtxKernelSpec` so relocatable compilation providers can link it.
3. Clamp the target compute capability to the forward-compatible family baseline (e.g. `sm_100f` on `sm_103a`) when the compilation provider's PTX ISA version is older than the GPU's compute capability.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017222142

display_title: PR #51088: [ROCm] Add libomp.so to the hipblaslt runtime data for ROCm 10.2 only!

head_commit.message:
PR #51088: [ROCm] Add libomp.so to the hipblaslt runtime data for ROCm 10.2 only!

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51088

## What

Add `rocm_path("lib/llvm/lib/libomp.so*")` to the `hipblaslt` runtime data in `third_party/gpus/rocm/BUILD.tpl`, next to `libtensilelite-host.so*`. The ROCm 10.2 release keeps this dependency; later ROCm builds no longer link OpenMP into `libtensilelite-host`.

## Why

In ROCm 10.2, `libhipblaslt.so.1` depends on `libtensilelite-host.so.1`, which needs `libomp.so` and finds it through `$ORIGIN/llvm/lib`. #50239 added `libtensilelite-host.so*` to the `hipblaslt` data but not `libomp.so`, so `rocm_dist/lib/llvm/lib/libomp.so` is missing from runfiles and anything that loads hipBLASLt from a 10.2 install fails before `main`:

```
error while loading shared libraries: libomp.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

This currently breaks the ROCm 10.2 nightly test runs, including the JAX unit tests in ROCm/xla's CI, where `xla_rocm_plugin.so` fails to load and every GPU test falls back to "Unknown backend: 'gpu'". ROCm 10.0 is unaffected because none of its math libraries need `libomp`.

## Testing

A `cc_test` depending on `@local_config_rocm//rocm:hipblaslt` that calls `dlopen("libhipblaslt.so.1", RTLD_NOW)`, built with `--config=rocm` and `ROCM_PATH` set to the TheRock pip install (`rocm-sdk path --root`), in the rocmless CI image:

| ROCm | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 10.2.0a20261016 | fails: `libomp.so: cannot open shared object file` | passes; `libomp.so` loads next to `libtensilelite-host.so.1` |
| 10.0.0 | n/a | passes |

End to end: jax-ml/jax `main` Bazel GPU tests (`build/rocm/ci_test_targets.txt`, `--//jax:build_jaxlib=wheel`, the ROCm/xla CI flags without RBE) on a local gfx950 with TheRock 10.2.0a20261016 from pip and this change applied via `--override_repository=xla`: 147 of 147 tests pass. Reverting this change, `//tests:cholesky_update_test_gpu` fails with `libomp.so: cannot open shared object file`, as in CI.

`--incompatible_disallow_empty_glob=false` is set in both XLA's and JAX's `.bazelrc`, so ROCm installs without `libomp` are unaffected.

Copybara import of the project:

display_title: Use CompilationProvider in CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx

head_commit.message:
Use CompilationProvider in CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx

`CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx` previously compiled PTX via `cuModuleLoadDataEx` on the single-threaded `cuda_driver` thread pool, which serialized PTX compilation across GPUs.

So this change replaces `LoadPtx` with a process-wide `CachingCompilationProvider` in `CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx` and loads the resulting CUBIN with `LoadCubin`. This avoids the single-threaded driver JIT and compiles each PTX module once per compute capability across all GPUs on a host.

Also:

1. Only retain `stream_exec_` in `CompilationProviderOptions` when driver compilation is enabled, and include `stream_exec_` in `operator==` so it matches `AbslHashValue`.
2. Remove the spurious `.extern` qualifier on the fixed-size `global_smem` array in `GetTmaPtxKernelSpec` so relocatable compilation providers can link it.
3. Clamp the target compute capability to the forward-compatible family baseline (e.g. `sm_100f` on `sm_103a`) when the compilation provider's PTX ISA version is older than the GPU's compute capability.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Forbid parameter-only reducers in Triton reduce support and fix reduce lowering

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Forbid parameter-only reducers in Triton reduce support

Lanes past the end of a tile are masked with the reduction's init value, which
assumes that the init value is neutral for the combiner. A combiner that just
returns one of its parameters, e.g. the `(a, b) -> b` combiner of a "take last"
reduction, has no such neutral value: every padded reduction dimension returned
the init value instead of the last element.

Forbid these computations in `CanTritonHandleReduce` so that the fusion falls
back to the native emitter, and keep the XTile emitter rejecting an empty
combiner body (`EmitReduceComputation`, `EmitScope`, `EmitCombinerStep`), so
that callers which bypass the support check fail with a status instead of
silently miscompiling padded tiles. The CPU tiled backend rejects these
combiners as well, so nothing is lost there.

Also fix the accumulator/element mapping in `LowerReduce`
(stablehlo_lower_to_triton.cc): the tt.reduce result plays the element, the
init value the accumulator. The previous mapping collapsed parameter-only
reducers to the init value.

Tests:
 - `SupportTest.ParameterOnlyReducerFailsGracefullyWithTriton` checks both the
   `Forbid` decision and that codegen rejects the computation.
 - `SoftmaxRewriterTritonTest.DoesNotFuseDiamondWithParameterOnlyReducer`
   covers the `reduce -> broadcast -> multiply` diamond of #50830.
 - `@reduce_with_parameter_only_reducer_and_non_neutral_init` pins down the
   `LowerReduce` argument mapping.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it for chunk-assigning heap algorithms, while keeping stats-only runs (`NoFragmentationStatsHeap` in `MinimumMemoryForModule`) restricted to direct operands so schedule scoring in `DefaultMemoryScheduler` does not change.

display_title: [XLA:GPU][Cleanup] Decide the enabled autotune backends in one place

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Decide the enabled autotune backends in one place

Which autotune backends are enabled was decided in three places: in
`ConfigAssignerPass::GetEnabledBackends`, in the instruction filter of
`ConfigAssignerPass` (which derived again from the flags whether the
block-level emitter is enabled), and in the scaled-dot checks of `GpuCompiler`.
Each copy implemented a different subset of the rules, so they could disagree.

Make `GetEnabledBackendTypes` the only place that decides which backends are
enabled, and use its result everywhere else:

- `ConfigAssignerPass::CreateBackends` creates the backends of the given types.
  It replaces `GetEnabledBackends`.
- `GetShouldAssignConfigToInstructionFn` takes the enabled backends.
- The scaled-dot checks of `GpuCompiler` check whether the `TRITON` or
  `CUDNN_FISSION` backend is enabled.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Wait on the host for cross-device events before enqueuing D2D copies.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Wait on the host for cross-device events before enqueuing D2D copies.

A D2D copy from GPU 0 to GPU 1 makes GPU 0's stream wait for an event on GPU 1.
If that event is stuck behind a collective on GPU 1 and a context-synchronizing
call (like cuModuleLoad) runs on GPU 0, GPU 0 can never launch its half of the collective, which creates a deadlock.

Waiting for the event asynchronously on the host instead keeps GPU 0's stream free, so GPU 0 can still launch its half of the collective.

The new behavior is off by default and behind `XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_WAIT_CROSS_DEVICE_COPIES=true`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Replace `PjRtRawBuffer::GetExternalDmaInfo()` with `AcquireExternalDmaAccess()`.

head_commit.message:
Replace `PjRtRawBuffer::GetExternalDmaInfo()` with `AcquireExternalDmaAccess()`.

`GetExternalDmaInfo()` (cl/1008163882) returns a raw buffer's offset and size
inside the backend's dma-buf, for external DMA engines such as NICs. Because
it is a one-shot query, PJRT never learns when the external engine is done
with that address. On TPU, HBM compaction can move an allocation whenever no
TPU DMA is using it; without knowing about the external DMA, compaction can
move the buffer out from under the NIC.

`AcquireExternalDmaAccess()` fixes this by returning a ref-counted handle
instead of the raw address:

```c++
class ExternalDmaAccess {
  virtual ~ExternalDmaAccess() = default;  // subclasses unpin here
  const ExternalDmaInfo& info() const;
};
virtual tsl::AsyncValueRef<ExternalDmaAccess> AcquireExternalDmaAccess();
```

The `AsyncValueRef` resolves once the buffer is allocated and its address is
fixed, and the access ends when the caller drops the last reference. A
follow-up CL implements this in `TpuRawBuffer` by pinning the HBM range
against compaction until `~ExternalDmaAccess()` runs.

On the C API side, `get_external_dma_info` (the last slot, no callers yet) is
replaced in place by `acquire_external_dma_access`, which returns a
`PJRT_ExternalDmaAccess` struct `{vtable, PJRT_DeviceEvent}`. The
`PJRT_DeviceEvent` signals when the access is established, `vtable->get_info`
reads `(fd, offset, size)`, and `vtable->destroy` ends the access. When client
and plugin live in the same binary, the client unwraps the underlying
`AsyncValue` directly with no extra allocation. `PjRtCApiRawBuffer` also
overrides `AcquireExternalDmaAccess()` to forward through the wrapped C raw
buffer.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017973590

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Wait on the host for cross-device events before enqueuing D2D copies.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Wait on the host for cross-device events before enqueuing D2D copies.

A D2D copy from GPU 0 to GPU 1 makes GPU 0's stream wait for an event on GPU 1.
If that event is stuck behind a collective on GPU 1 and a context-synchronizing
call (like cuModuleLoad) runs on GPU 0, GPU 0 can never launch its half of the collective, which creates a deadlock.

Waiting for the event asynchronously on the host instead keeps GPU 0's stream free, so GPU 0 can still launch its half of the collective.

The new behavior is off by default and behind `XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_WAIT_CROSS_DEVICE_COPIES=true`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it for chunk-assigning heap algorithms, while keeping stats-only runs (`NoFragmentationStatsHeap` in `MinimumMemoryForModule`) restricted to direct operands so schedule scoring in `DefaultMemoryScheduler` does not change.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Replace `PjRtRawBuffer::GetExternalDmaInfo()` with `AcquireExternalDmaAccess()`.

head_commit.message:
Replace `PjRtRawBuffer::GetExternalDmaInfo()` with `AcquireExternalDmaAccess()`.

`GetExternalDmaInfo()` (cl/1008163882) returns a raw buffer's offset and size
inside the backend's dma-buf, for external DMA engines such as NICs. Because
it is a one-shot query, PJRT never learns when the external engine is done
with that address. On TPU, HBM compaction can move an allocation whenever no
TPU DMA is using it; without knowing about the external DMA, compaction can
move the buffer out from under the NIC.

`AcquireExternalDmaAccess()` fixes this by returning a ref-counted handle
instead of the raw address:

```c++
class ExternalDmaAccess {
  virtual ~ExternalDmaAccess() = default;  // subclasses unpin here
  const ExternalDmaInfo& info() const;
};
virtual tsl::AsyncValueRef<ExternalDmaAccess> AcquireExternalDmaAccess();
```

The `AsyncValueRef` resolves once the buffer is allocated and its address is
fixed, and the access ends when the caller drops the last reference. A
follow-up CL implements this in `TpuRawBuffer` by pinning the HBM range
against compaction until `~ExternalDmaAccess()` runs.

On the C API side, `get_external_dma_info` (the last slot, no callers yet) is
replaced in place by `acquire_external_dma_access`, which returns a
`PJRT_ExternalDmaAccess` struct `{vtable, PJRT_DeviceEvent}`. The
`PJRT_DeviceEvent` signals when the access is established, `vtable->get_info`
reads `(fd, offset, size)`, and `vtable->destroy` ends the access. When client
and plugin live in the same binary, the client unwraps the underlying
`AsyncValue` directly with no extra allocation. `PjRtCApiRawBuffer` also
overrides `AcquireExternalDmaAccess()` to forward through the wrapped C raw
buffer.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1011845566

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Reclaim freed scratch allocations in RAFT select_k FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Reclaim freed scratch allocations in RAFT select_k FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource

FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource in xla/backends/gpu/runtime/select_k_exec_raft_impl.h previously implemented do_deallocate as a no-op monotonic bump allocator. When raft::matrix::select_k runs a radix-based algorithm (kRadix8bits, kRadix11bits, kRadix11bitsExtraPass) with sorted=true, Phase 1 (radix::select_k) frees all of its temporary buffers before Phase 2 (segmented_sort_by_key) allocates output buffers and CUB DeviceSegmentedRadixSort temporary storage. Because offset_ was never rewound, Phase 2 allocated on top of Phase 1 (Phase1 + Phase2 instead of max(Phase1, Phase2)).

Updates FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource to track live allocations, unwind LIFO deallocations from the top of the buffer, and reset offset_ to 0 when live_allocations_ == 0. Since all operations in select_k_exec execute sequentially on the single CUDA stream bound to RaftStreamResource, reusing offset 0 across phases is stream-safe (including under CUDA Graph / CommandBuffer capture and replay).

Examples before/after:
```
(batch=256, n=16384, k=512) (kRadix8bits): 4.001 MB → 2.001 MB (-49.98%)
(batch=1024, n=32768, k=512) (kRadix8bits): 15.504 MB → 8.004 MB (-48.37%, -7.50 MB)
(batch=512, n=32768, k=512) (kRadix11bits): 11.502 MB → 7.500 MB (-34.80%, -4.00 MB)
(batch=1024, n=65536, k=512) (kRadix8bits): 23.004 MB → 15.000 MB (-34.80%, -8.00 MB)
```

display_title: [TF] Switch TensorFlow default build to Bzlmod and sync MODULE.bazel.

head_commit.message:
[TF] Switch TensorFlow default build to Bzlmod and sync MODULE.bazel.

Following the Bazel 8.8.2 upgrade, enable `--enable_bzlmod` and `--noenable_workspace` by default in TensorFlow while adding `--config=workspace` as a fallback configuration and flipping `ci/official/envs/bzlmod` to `--config workspace` so `WORKSPACE` continues to be tested in CI for downstream consumers. display_title: Add post-scheduling control dependencies to async callers in CopyRemover.

head_commit.message:
Add post-scheduling control dependencies to async callers in CopyRemover.

When `CopyRemover::TryElideCopy` runs with `insert_post_scheduling_control_dependencies=true`, `LiveRangeBefore` (via `HloOrdering::UsesBeforeValueDefinition`) resolves instructions inside an async wrapped computation (`IsAsyncComputation()`) to their `kAsyncStart` caller in the parent computation when checking whether uses of `src` execute before the definition of `dst`. However, `AddControlDependenciesBetween` previously checked `use->instruction->parent() != dst->value->instruction()->parent()` directly on the inner async computation instruction and skipped adding the control dependency whenever `src` or `dst` lived inside an async computation.

Without that control dependency from the last use of `src` to the `kAsyncStart` caller of `dst`, later passes such as `HloRematerialization` could rematerialize a reader of `src` after `kAsyncStart` / `kAsyncDone` had already overwritten the shared buffer.

Resolve instructions in async computations to their `kAsyncStart` caller in `AddControlDependenciesBetween`, and verify `ordering_->ExecutesBefore(use_inst, dst_inst)` so that in-place async operations (where `src->uses` includes the `kAsyncDone` / `kAsyncUpdate` instruction) do not add a backward control edge to `kAsyncStart`.

display_title: PR #51088: [ROCm] Add libomp.so to the hipblaslt runtime data for ROCm 10.2 only!

head_commit.message:
PR #51088: [ROCm] Add libomp.so to the hipblaslt runtime data for ROCm 10.2 only!

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51088

## What

Add `rocm_path("lib/llvm/lib/libomp.so*")` to the `hipblaslt` runtime data in `third_party/gpus/rocm/BUILD.tpl`, next to `libtensilelite-host.so*`. The ROCm 10.2 release keeps this dependency; later ROCm builds no longer link OpenMP into `libtensilelite-host`.

## Why

In ROCm 10.2, `libhipblaslt.so.1` depends on `libtensilelite-host.so.1`, which needs `libomp.so` and finds it through `$ORIGIN/llvm/lib`. #50239 added `libtensilelite-host.so*` to the `hipblaslt` data but not `libomp.so`, so `rocm_dist/lib/llvm/lib/libomp.so` is missing from runfiles and anything that loads hipBLASLt from a 10.2 install fails before `main`:

```
error while loading shared libraries: libomp.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

This currently breaks the ROCm 10.2 nightly test runs, including the JAX unit tests in ROCm/xla's CI, where `xla_rocm_plugin.so` fails to load and every GPU test falls back to "Unknown backend: 'gpu'". ROCm 10.0 is unaffected because none of its math libraries need `libomp`.

## Testing

A `cc_test` depending on `@local_config_rocm//rocm:hipblaslt` that calls `dlopen("libhipblaslt.so.1", RTLD_NOW)`, built with `--config=rocm` and `ROCM_PATH` set to the TheRock pip install (`rocm-sdk path --root`), in the rocmless CI image:

| ROCm | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 10.2.0a20261016 | fails: `libomp.so: cannot open shared object file` | passes; `libomp.so` loads next to `libtensilelite-host.so.1` |
| 10.0.0 | n/a | passes |

End to end: jax-ml/jax `main` Bazel GPU tests (`build/rocm/ci_test_targets.txt`, `--//jax:build_jaxlib=wheel`, the ROCm/xla CI flags without RBE) on a local gfx950 with TheRock 10.2.0a20261016 from pip and this change applied via `--override_repository=xla`: 147 of 147 tests pass. Reverting this change, `//tests:cholesky_update_test_gpu` fails with `libomp.so: cannot open shared object file`, as in CI.

`--incompatible_disallow_empty_glob=false` is set in both XLA's and JAX's `.bazelrc`, so ROCm installs without `libomp` are unaffected.

display_title: PR #129734: Add tf.experimental.numpy diff prepend/append support with NumPy semantics

head_commit.message:
PR #129734: Add tf.experimental.numpy diff prepend/append support with NumPy semantics

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/pull/129734

NumPy's `np.diff` accepts optional `prepend`/`append` values that are added along `axis` before the differences run:

```
>>> np.diff(np.array([1, 2, 3]), prepend=0)
array([1, 1, 1])

>>> np.diff(np.array([1, 2, 3]), append=5)
array([1, 1, 2])
```

The tf-numpy wrapper lacked both parameters entirely: `tnp.diff(a, prepend=0)` raises `TypeError: diff() got an unexpected keyword argument 'prepend'`.

Mirror NumPy's implementation in `np_math_ops.diff`:

- A scalar (0-d) `prepend`/`append` is broadcast to length 1 along `axis` and all other dimensions of `a` (NumPy's `_broadcast_to` on `shape` with `shape[axis] = 1`) and concatenated once, before the `n` differences run.
- An array `prepend`/`append` is concatenated as-is; when both shapes are statically known, a dimension mismatch outside `axis` raises NumPy's exact `ValueError: all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match exactly` instead of the backend's `InvalidArgumentError`.
- The two sides are promoted to a shared dtype with `np_utils.result_type` before concatenating, like NumPy's concatenate promotes (e.g. `np.diff(int32, prepend=1.5)` yields float64).
- Boolean inputs keep the boolean (`!=`) difference semantics when the promoted dtype is still boolean.

Tests extend `testDiff`: scalar `prepend`/`append` (including `n=2` with both boundaries), array `prepend` with `axis=0` and array `append` with `axis=1` matched against `np.diff`, the mixed-dtype promotion case, the boolean-boundary case, and a mismatch outside `axis` raising NumPy's ValueError.

Signed-off-by: Kaivalya Singh <singh.kaivalya@gmail.com>

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Reclaim freed scratch allocations in RAFT select_k FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Reclaim freed scratch allocations in RAFT select_k FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource

FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource in xla/backends/gpu/runtime/select_k_exec_raft_impl.h previously implemented do_deallocate as a no-op monotonic bump allocator. When raft::matrix::select_k runs a radix-based algorithm (kRadix8bits, kRadix11bits, kRadix11bitsExtraPass) with sorted=true, Phase 1 (radix::select_k) frees all of its temporary buffers before Phase 2 (segmented_sort_by_key) allocates output buffers and CUB DeviceSegmentedRadixSort temporary storage. Because offset_ was never rewound, Phase 2 allocated on top of Phase 1 (Phase1 + Phase2 instead of max(Phase1, Phase2)).

Updates FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource to track live allocations, unwind LIFO deallocations from the top of the buffer, and reset offset_ to 0 when live_allocations_ == 0. Since all operations in select_k_exec execute sequentially on the single CUDA stream bound to RaftStreamResource, reusing offset 0 across phases is stream-safe (including under CUDA Graph / CommandBuffer capture and replay).

Examples:
```
(batch=256, n=16384, k=512) (kRadix8bits): 4.001 MB → 2.001 MB (-49.98%)
(batch=1024, n=32768, k=512) (kRadix8bits): 15.504 MB → 8.004 MB (-48.37%, -7.50 MB)
(batch=512, n=32768, k=512) (kRadix11bits): 11.502 MB → 7.500 MB (-34.80%, -4.00 MB)
(batch=1024, n=65536, k=512) (kRadix8bits): 23.004 MB → 15.000 MB (-34.80%, -8.00 MB)
```

display_title: PR #129734: Add tf.experimental.numpy diff prepend/append support with NumPy semantics

head_commit.message:
PR #129734: Add tf.experimental.numpy diff prepend/append support with NumPy semantics

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/pull/129734

NumPy's `np.diff` accepts optional `prepend`/`append` values that are added along `axis` before the differences run:

```
>>> np.diff(np.array([1, 2, 3]), prepend=0)
array([1, 1, 1])

>>> np.diff(np.array([1, 2, 3]), append=5)
array([1, 1, 2])
```

The tf-numpy wrapper lacked both parameters entirely: `tnp.diff(a, prepend=0)` raises `TypeError: diff() got an unexpected keyword argument 'prepend'`.

Mirror NumPy's implementation in `np_math_ops.diff`:

- A scalar (0-d) `prepend`/`append` is broadcast to length 1 along `axis` and all other dimensions of `a` (NumPy's `_broadcast_to` on `shape` with `shape[axis] = 1`) and concatenated once, before the `n` differences run.
- An array `prepend`/`append` is concatenated as-is; when both shapes are statically known, a dimension mismatch outside `axis` raises NumPy's exact `ValueError: all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match exactly` instead of the backend's `InvalidArgumentError`.
- The two sides are promoted to a shared dtype with `np_utils.result_type` before concatenating, like NumPy's concatenate promotes (e.g. `np.diff(int32, prepend=1.5)` yields float64).
- Boolean inputs keep the boolean (`!=`) difference semantics when the promoted dtype is still boolean.

Tests extend `testDiff`: scalar `prepend`/`append` (including `n=2` with both boundaries), array `prepend` with `axis=0` and array `append` with `axis=1` matched against `np.diff`, the mixed-dtype promotion case, the boolean-boundary case, and a mismatch outside `axis` raising NumPy's ValueError.

Signed-off-by: Kaivalya Singh <singh.kaivalya@gmail.com>

Copybara import of the project:

--

display_title: Match StableSortExpander-expanded sort comparators in xla::TopkRewriter

head_commit.message:
Match StableSortExpander-expanded sort comparators in xla::TopkRewriter

When `StableSortExpander` runs before `TopkRewriter` (for example, in a
post-SPMD simplification pass), a stable TopK `kSort` has `is_stable=false`
and its comparator root is wrapped in `Select(Eq(old_root, cloned_root),
Lt(Parameter(2), Parameter(3)), old_root)`, where `cloned_root` computes the
same key comparison with swapped parameters `(1, 0)`. Extend `MatchNanSafeGt`
in `xla/service/topk_rewriter.cc` to verify both `old_root` and `cloned_root`
and preserve `is_stable = true` on the resulting `TopK` custom call in
`CreateTopKCustomCall`, while clearing incompatible tiled sharding on `topk`,
`value_gte`, and `index_gte` when reshaping `>2D` or transposing 2D
`sort_dim == 0` sorts.

`AdvancedMatchShapeCoveringDynamicIndexInstruction` in `xla/service/while_loop_unroller.cc` previously allocated `std::vector<bool> indices_covered(dimension_size)`, marked covered indices element-by-element across each slice, and scanned `indices_covered` with a 32-bit `int index` loop. display_title: [XLA:GPU] [2/2] Unroll and vectorize kLoop reductions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] [2/2] Unroll and vectorize kLoop reductions.

***Problem:*** `kLoop` fusions that loop over a small reduction dimension (e.g. split-K factors below the warp size) never get vectorized loads and stores, because the unroll factor is sized only from the small output element count and `VectorizeLoadsAndStoresPass` runs before the inner reduction loop is unrolled, so it only sees that non-unit-stride loop.

***Solution:*** Allow unrolling up to `MaxUnrollFactor` (while keeping enough threads to fill the GPU) when the fusion contains a `kReduce` whose operand alone can saturate the GPU, unroll only the inner reduction loops before `VectorizeLoadsAndStoresPass` so the outer unroll loop becomes the innermost vectorizable loop, and teach `lower_tensors` to infer access alignment from `xla.apply_indexing` indices.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] [1/2] Sink reduce through unstrided slice consumers.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] [1/2] Sink reduce through unstrided slice consumers.

***Problem:*** When `DotMerger` packs several dots into one and `SplitkRewriter` then splits that dot, the split-K `reduce` feeds unstrided `slice` ops that extract each original dot's result, so it can only be fused into those slices via the slow naive `kLoop` emitter (small split-K) or not at all (large split-K).

***Solution:*** In `GpuAlgebraicSimplifier`, when every consumer of a `reduce` maps to a contiguous unstrided `slice` (optionally through unary elementwise, `bitcast`, or `reshape` ops) and the slices together cover no more elements than the `reduce` output, replace each `slice` chain with a `reduce` over the correspondingly sliced input followed by the replayed passthrough ops so each original dot gets its own reduction without reducing or reading more elements.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Flush L2 and average timed runs when autotuning on GPU.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Flush L2 and average timed runs when autotuning on GPU.

***Problem:*** `GpuProfiler` times each autotuning candidate once right after a warm-up run, so operands remain L2-resident and timer quantization hides cold-cache execution differences, making config selection noisy across compilations.

***Solution:*** Overwrite a scratch buffer twice the L2 cache size before each timed run and report the mean across `xla_gpu_autotune_num_timed_runs` timed runs when autotuning is enabled and `xla_gpu_autotune_flush_l2_cache` is set.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Wake waiting threads in FIFO order in xla::Semaphore::Acquire.

head_commit.message:
Wake waiting threads in FIFO order in xla::Semaphore::Acquire.

When a multi-model TPU inference server is under heavy concurrency and hits its
max in-flight computation limit (`max_inflight_computations_semaphore_`),
incoming requests block on `xla::Semaphore::Acquire`. Because `Acquire` waited
on `absl::Mutex::LockWhen` without tracking arrival order, releasing capacity
woke arbitrary waiting threads rather than the oldest waiting request, allowing
newly arrived requests to repeatedly jump ahead of older requests and causing
severe tail-latency starvation.

* Guard the new FIFO behavior behind `--xla_pjrt_fifo_semaphore` (default `false`).
* Track blocked callers in a singly-linked FIFO queue of stack-allocated `Waiter`
  nodes (`head_` / `tail_`) with per-waiter `absl::CondVar`. Capacity returned
  in `Release` is handed off directly to queued waiters in arrival order.
* `TryAcquire` avoids barging ahead of queued waiters (`head_ == nullptr`) while
  allowing smaller acquisitions to bypass earlier unsatisfied larger requests.
* Use a lock-free fast-fail check in `TryAcquire` and an adaptive user-space
  pre-spin in `Acquire` before enqueuing a `Waiter` and sleeping on `CondVar`.

Tested with `bazel test //xla/pjrt:semaphore_test`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Propagate runtime execution timeouts when loading AOT executables.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Propagate runtime execution timeouts when loading AOT executables.

Execution timeouts (`xla_gpu_execution_terminate_timeout`, `xla_gpu_device_execution_terminate_timeout`, `xla_gpu_execution_progress_tracking`, `xla_gpu_executable_warn_stuck_timeout_seconds`, and `xla_gpu_executable_terminate_timeout_seconds`) previously did not take effect on AOT-compiled GPU executables with embedded HLO module configs:

1. `StreamExecutorExecutable::SerializeExecutable` serializes compile-time `ExecutableBuildOptionsProto` (including compile-time `DebugOptions`, where timeouts default to `"inf"`, and `env_option_overrides`). When `StreamExecutorExecutable::Deserialize` is called with `options = std::nullopt`, `compile_options.executable_build_options.has_debug_options()` is true (or materialized by `ApplyAllOptionOverrides()`), causing `LocalClient::LoadInternal` to pass serialized compile-time `DebugOptions` instead of `GetDebugOptionsFromFlags()`. Additionally, running `ApplyAllOptionOverrides()` after flag overrides would let serialized compile-time `env_option_overrides` clobber serving-time flags.
2. `GpuExecutable::ModuleConfigMetadataFromProto` and `GpuExecutable::FromProto` only copied `xla_dump_to` and `xla_gpu_experimental_nccl_window_symmetric` from the load-time `DebugOptions` into `runtime_debug_options_` and the embedded `HloModule`, leaving the timeout fields at their compile-time values (`"inf"`).

Extract `ApplyLoadTimeDebugOptionsOverrides` into `debug_options_flags` and invoke `CompileOptions::ApplyAllOptionOverrides()` before load-time flag overrides in `StreamExecutorExecutable::Deserialize(..., std::nullopt)`, propagate the same overrides in `GpuExecutable::ModuleConfigMetadataFromProto` and `GpuExecutable::FromProto`, and preserve the standard `10s` / `30s` rendezvous timeout defaults when those fields are unset on a default-constructed `DebugOptions`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Reclaim freed scratch allocations in RAFT select_k FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Reclaim freed scratch allocations in RAFT select_k FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource

FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource in xla/backends/gpu/runtime/select_k_exec_raft_impl.h previously implemented do_deallocate as a no-op monotonic bump allocator. When raft::matrix::select_k runs a radix-based algorithm (kRadix8bits, kRadix11bits, kRadix11bitsExtraPass) with sorted=true, Phase 1 (radix::select_k) frees all of its temporary buffers before Phase 2 (segmented_sort_by_key) allocates output buffers and CUB DeviceSegmentedRadixSort temporary storage. Because offset_ was never rewound, Phase 2 allocated on top of Phase 1 (Phase1 + Phase2 instead of max(Phase1, Phase2)).

Updates FixedBufferDeviceMemoryResource to track live allocations, unwind LIFO deallocations from the top of the buffer, and reset offset_ to 0 when live_allocations_ == 0. Since all operations in select_k_exec execute sequentially on the single CUDA stream bound to RaftStreamResource, reusing offset 0 across phases is stream-safe (including under CUDA Graph / CommandBuffer capture and replay).

Examples before/after:
```
(batch=256, n=16384, k=512) (kRadix8bits): 4.001 MB → 2.001 MB (-49.98%)
(batch=1024, n=32768, k=512) (kRadix8bits): 15.504 MB → 8.004 MB (-48.37%, -7.50 MB)
(batch=512, n=32768, k=512) (kRadix11bits): 11.502 MB → 7.500 MB (-34.80%, -4.00 MB)
(batch=1024, n=65536, k=512) (kRadix8bits): 23.004 MB → 15.000 MB (-34.80%, -8.00 MB)
```

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Wake waiting threads in FIFO order in xla::Semaphore::Acquire.

head_commit.message:
Wake waiting threads in FIFO order in xla::Semaphore::Acquire.

When a multi-model TPU inference server is under heavy concurrency and hits its
max in-flight computation limit (`max_inflight_computations_semaphore_`),
incoming requests block on `xla::Semaphore::Acquire`. Because `Acquire` waited
on `absl::Mutex::LockWhen` without tracking arrival order, releasing capacity
woke arbitrary waiting threads rather than the oldest waiting request, allowing
newly arrived requests to repeatedly jump ahead of older requests and causing
severe tail-latency starvation.

* Guard the new FIFO behavior behind `--xla_pjrt_fifo_semaphore` (default `false`).
* Track blocked callers in a singly-linked FIFO queue of stack-allocated `Waiter`
  nodes (`head_` / `tail_`) with per-waiter `absl::CondVar`. Capacity returned
  in `Release` is handed off directly to queued waiters in arrival order.
* `TryAcquire` avoids barging ahead of queued waiters (`head_ == nullptr`) while
  allowing smaller acquisitions to bypass earlier unsatisfied larger requests.
* Use a lock-free fast-fail check in `TryAcquire` and an adaptive user-space
  pre-spin in `Acquire` before enqueuing a `Waiter` and sleeping on `CondVar`.

Tested with `bazel test //xla/pjrt:semaphore_test`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Track covered interval end in AdvancedMatchShapeCoveringDynamicIndexInstruction

`AdvancedMatchShapeCoveringDynamicIndexInstruction` in `xla/service/while_loop_unroller.cc` previously allocated `std::vector<bool> indices_covered(dimension_size)`, marked covered indices element-by-element across each slice, and scanned `indices_covered` with a 32-bit `int index` loop. When `dimension_size > INT32_MAX`, `int index` overflows 32-bit signed `int` and materializing/scanning `dimension_size` bits takes `O(dimension_size)` memory and time even for a 2-iteration loop updating large slices.

Since `start_index_value` advances by a positive step and clamping is monotonic, track the contiguous covered prefix `[0, covered_until)` in `int64_t` across loop iterations instead of allocating and scanning a per-element bit vector.
